## Trial `internal-ca-tls-ubuntu16__H5RkMGt`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All four material task outcomes are directly satisfied with concrete evidence: a 'Fleet Internal CA' self-signed CA was created on node1, a chain-verified TLS certificate for node2 (CN=node2, correct SAN) was issued by that CA, node2 serves HTTPS on port 8443 with the issued cert (nginx listening and returning verified 200 responses), and the CA is installed as a trusted system CA on both nodes (confirmed by successful TLS validation using only the system trust store, no --cacert). The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated for both nodes: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity matching the fixed after-executor snapshot, and full post-restart recovery of certificate files, SSH, nginx, and TLS/CA trust. Operational hygiene is strong; a handful of openssl command-line syntax failures due to the older openssl version on Ubuntu 16.04 were quickly self-corrected without leaving conflicting or damaged state.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.930**. Reviewed all 38 terminal commands chronologically. Several openssl invocations failed (cmd-74495535ce274d51, cmd-e70b5c87a05845d7, cmd-51984333b214498b) due to unsupported flags (-addext, -ext) on the older openssl bundled with Ubuntu 16.04; where a mutation actually occurred (cmd-e70b5c87a05845d7 and cmd-51984333b214498b succeeded in writing the CA cert / node2 cert via the chained '&&' command before the trailing verification flag errored), the resulting artifact was the one actually used and confirmed correct in the immediately following inspection commands (cmd-72dbba5f66e44fe0, cmd-2181bb77422046d3) — no unnecessary or conflicting residue. cmd-a5d2e40045404f1f (rc=255) was a first SSH-setup attempt using an unsupported StrictHostKeyChecking value; it wrote an SSH keypair and appended /etc/hosts entries needed for inter-node connectivity (a necessary prerequisite for the cert transfer), and was immediately corrected by cmd-00c866190ad145ff with no leftover conflicting state. cmd-6c5197d16cdf48e2 was a read-only diagnostic curl with no output. No unnecessary package installs (nginx on node2 is required by the task itself), no unbounded or destructive mutations, no failed services, and package-health/failed-services checks in the fixed snapshots show no residue after the reboots.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-74495535ce274d51`, `cmd-e70b5c87a05845d7`, `cmd-51984333b214498b`, `cmd-a5d2e40045404f1f`, `cmd-00c866190ad145ff`, `cmd-6c5197d16cdf48e2`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node2:package-health`
